invariants: Only the exact bridge-owned Agent/Session and a present callId can answer machine permissions; same-id foreign Agents and identity-free requests delegate.
The committed tool update drains before the actual outgoing session/request_permission request; the request advertises exactly allow-once and reject-once choices.

A selected allow-once grants only this decision; unknown choices reject, explicit cancellation cancels, and disconnected or malformed peers fail closed through ApprovalService and retain paired audit records.
Pending decisions retain actual RPC correlation and close ownership; real canonical Agent/tool/next-request process consumers must be verified before integration.
identity: Exact Agent object, exact owned Session, protocol tool-call identity and outgoing typed request id.
ownership: Bridge-owned ordered updates and outgoing RPC; ApprovalService owns per-decision audit and caller cancellation.
ordering: Committed tool update before permission request; peer answer before per-action execution and audit completion.
errors: Remote errors/connection close/malformed response never grant; foreign or identity-free requests use downstream answerers.
cancellation: Caller cancellation remains ApprovalService-owned; RPC close rejects pending peer responses. No persistent approval policy is inferred.
adaptation: Python 3.8 async waterfall, exact object ownership and an owned asyncio.Event cancellation adapter for canonical Agent tools. The separately reviewed UPSTREAM-ACP-PERMISSION-001 predicate accepts only two fixed malformed grant responses; earlier eight predicates and C58 are unchanged.
